extracted.intended_audience: NADCRC council members, NIDCR staff, and other NIH/NIDCR stakeholders involved in second-level review and program planning
extracted.subtask_description: Operating procedures for the National Advisory Dental and Craniofacial Research Council describing membership rules, the second-level review of grant applications, voting options, expedited electronic review, concept clearance, intramural reporting, staff authorities, emergency procedures, and related governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council purpose and focus for second-level review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council has responsibility of advising, consulting with, and making recommendations to the Secretary, HHS and the Director, NIDCR on directions of research, research support, training, and career development; included is the conduct of the second level review of Summary Statements of grant applications with a focus on NIDCR scientific program priorities and program balance as well as the conduct of research by the Division of Intramural Research, NIDCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-level review emphasizes institute program priorities and program balance rather than re-scoring scientific merit assigned by SRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council membership composition and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Council will consist of not more than 18 members appointed by the Secretary and at least five nonvoting ex officio members (Secretary HHS; Director NIH; Director NIDCR; Under Secretary for Health or Chief Dental Director at VA; Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs or designees). The Secretary selects the Chair and appoints 13 members whose training and interests prepare them to serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointed members serve four-year terms, not eligible for reappointment to the same Council until two years after expiration; a member may serve for 180 days after term expiration or until replacement selected. A quorum consists of a majority of currently appointed members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of applications for Council second-level review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council provides second level review of Summary Statements for all research grant, conference grant, program project, cooperative agreement, institutional training, and career development award applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the exception of expedited and en bloc review, specific actions/applications considered individually include MERIT awards; special staff or council actions; eligible-for-funding applications from foreign PI/MPI institutions; applications with pending concerns re: human subjects, animal welfare, inclusion; biohazard concerns; applications from investigators with > $2.0M total NIH/NIDCR support; multiple-PI applications when any PI has > $2.0M; applications of special interest or policy issues; unresolved appeals of peer review; Phase III clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of primary and secondary Council reviewers for special actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, two Council members are assigned as primary and secondary reviewers for any special actions; following a staff presentation, they lead Council discussion and vote to approve or disapprove final recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other applications (not special actions) will be voted on en bloc by Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: En bloc voting for routine applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All other applications (not identified as special actions) will be voted on en bloc by Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications placed en bloc are considered together rather than discussed individually unless pulled for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDCR staff delegated authorities for certain reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDCR staff members are authorized to provide secondary review of all individual fellowships (F30, F31, F32, and F33). This review is conducted by the Executive Staff of NIDCR, documented in minutes, included in the official grant file, and reported to the Council for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff actions on fellowships are informational to Council and do not require Council concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff authority for administrative supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDCR staff may review and approve or disapprove administrative supplements to existing grants up to $250,000 in direct costs provided the supplement does not expand the scope of the scientific aims of the parent award or expand the scope of the scientific aims of the ongoing project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delegation is limited by scope-change prohibition; staff must ensure supplements do not alter the project's scientific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council voting options and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council may not change the scores assigned by the SRG. Available voting options: concurrence with the SRG recommendations; non-concurrence based on scientific/technical merit (application may be deferred for SRG reconsideration); non-concurrence based on considerations other than scientific/technical merit (e.g., appropriateness of SRG membership; mismatch between percentile/priority score and written summary); deferral to obtain additional information for Council consideration at a subsequent meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council members wishing to discuss an application should contact the Executive Secretary well in advance so staff can provide background and modify the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff considerations when adjusting funding plans
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDCR staff options are consistent with the institute’s policy of adjusting funding plans during the fiscal year to fill scientific gaps, avoid potential scientific overlap with current awards, and consider an applicant’s new/early-stage investigator status and level of other support available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may use these programmatic considerations to prioritize or reprioritize funding recommendations within NIH/NIDCR policy constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff authority for budget adjustments and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDCR staff may adjust recommended budgets upward or downward for any application. Upward adjustments may not be made for the purpose of expansion of scientific aims or altering scientific content/scope. Downward adjustments are intended so proposed research can still be conducted but in a cost-effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff will report budget adjustments exceeding $100,000 in direct costs at the next Council meeting for informational purposes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for expedited second-level review (ECB)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most meritorious Summary Statements for R, U-, P-, T-, and K-series can undergo expedited Council review immediately following an SRG meeting and prior to the next Council meeting, provided the applications are from domestic institutions and have: scores or percentiles within the institute’s funding range; summary statements available; no foreign components; no SRG-identified concerns regarding protection of human subjects, representation of gender/children/minorities, care and use of vertebrate animals, biohazards (hazardous materials/procedures, biosafety/biocontainment/security of Select Agents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited review is limited to applications meeting all listed eligibility conditions and is intended to accelerate funding of meritorious, non-problematic applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited electronic review process and voting options
rubrics_metrics.description: All Council members are asked to complete the expedited review via the Early Concurrence Module of the Electronic Council Book (ECB). Members have a minimum of 72 business hours to complete review by electronic voting. Voting options: concurrence with the initial scientific peer review; non-concurrence with the initial scientific peer review; or deferral for discussion by the full Council (no option for further deferral or re-review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for those in conflict of interest, all Council members have access to summary statements; members may comment directly in the ECB if concerns are noted. Applications receiving a majority of concurrence votes are considered for expedited funding. A report of en bloc applications undergoing expedited review is presented at the next Council meeting for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest access restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for those in Conflict of Interest (COI), all Council members have access to the summary statements provided to voting members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members with COI are excluded from access and voting on affected applications per NIH conflict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept clearance process and Council actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept clearance is the process to receive public advice on the merits of potential initiatives (concepts for proposed NOFOs). Concepts present objectives, rationale, and scientific needs/opportunities; no requirement exists to develop a concept into a NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two Council members serve as primary and secondary reviewers for each concept. After discussion, Council may vote: approval with or without modifications; disapproval; or deferral for further development and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intramural research reporting to Council
rubrics_metrics.description: At the January and May meetings during a closed session, the Board of Scientific Counselors (BSC) reports to the Council on outcomes of BSC reviews, with written reports and the Scientific Director’s response presented; the BSC Chair provides a verbal summary and the Scientific Director provides a verbal summary of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since these reports are informational for Council, no vote is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency procedures for Council meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an emergency would preclude the usual Council meeting, NIDCR staff may: consider only closed-session items focusing on a subset of Summary Statements; utilize the ECB with electronic voting/approvals for concurrence of Summary Statements (including Late Summary Statements); organize a fully electronic/virtual conference; or relocate the meeting to another site/date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council Executive Secretary, in consultation with the Director and senior staff, will communicate altered procedures and meeting arrangements to Council members and institute staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to review and revise Council operating procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: At any Council meeting, Council may review and approve the Operating Procedures for the NADCRC and make recommendations for revision where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating procedures are living governance documents and may be updated by Council action.
